library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Li and An (2025) built a semi-mechanistic parent-metabolite population PK model
for delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), its active metabolite
11-hydroxy-THC (11-OH-THC) and its terminal metabolite 11-nor-9-carboxy-THC
(THC-COOH), aimed at oral cannabis users, and used it to ask how well the
whole-blood THC "per se" limits of 1, 2 and 5 ng/mL used in some US states
separate impaired from unimpaired drivers.

- Citation: Li P, An G. Evaluation of Cannabis Per Se Laws: A Semi-Mechanistic
  Pharmacometrics Model for Quantitative Characterization of THC and
  Metabolites in Oral Users. *J Clin Pharmacol*. 2025;65(5):535.
  [doi:10.1002/jcph.6181](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.6181)
- Model file: `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Li_2025_tetrahydrocannabinol.R`

The structure (Figure 1, Equations 1-11) is:

- **THC**: first-order absorption from an oral `depot` with bioavailability
  F; `central` plus two peripheral compartments; the second peripheral
  compartment exchanges with an `adipose` compartment through a
  permeability-surface-area product PS and an adipose:plasma partition
  coefficient KP.
- **11-OH-THC**: formed from the whole of THC clearance; the same
  central / two peripheral / adipose structure with its own PS2 and KP2.
- **THC-COOH**: formed from a fraction Fm of 11-OH-THC clearance (the
  remainder is excreted unchanged); two compartments.

Formation is 1:1 by mass. The authors deliberately fitted weight-based rather
than molar concentrations because the molecular weights differ by less than 5%
per metabolic step (Methods, Data Source), so no molecular-weight ratio
appears in the model.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Li_2025_tetrahydrocannabinol")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui)
```

# Population

The model was fitted to **digitised mean concentration-time profiles**, not
to individual data: 25 dose groups from 10 published studies (Supplement
Table S2), seven oral (single doses of 5-90 mg as dronabinol capsules,
cannabis decoction, brownies, commercial edibles or hemp oil) and three
intravenous (1.6-5 mg). Sampling ran from 4 to 54 h after dose. Only
occasional users were included (the frequent-user arms of Newmeyer 2016 and
2017 were dropped) and only fasted administration (the fed arm of Lunn 2019 was
dropped). Four studies measured whole blood, which the authors converted to
plasma with blood:plasma ratios of 0.71 (THC), 0.73 (11-OH-THC) and 0.65
(THC-COOH).

Because the data were study means, inter-individual variability could not be
estimated. The four random effects in the model (on the THC, 11-OH-THC and
THC-COOH central volumes and on THC clearance) are **inter-study**
variabilities; simulating from them gives a between-study spread that the
paper itself used as its "virtual subject" variability in the per se
analysis.

| Q2, V_THC,peri2 | 29.7 L/h, 88.3 L | Table 1 |
| PS, V_THC,adipose, KP | 5.5 L/h, 91.8 L, 14 | Table 1 |

# Typical-value profiles (Figure 2)

Figure 2 overlays the population-predicted (typical-value) profiles on the
digitised study means for single oral doses of 10, 20, 45 and 50 mg.

```{r fig2}
fig2_doses <- c(10, 20, 45, 50)
fig2_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.1), seq(12.5, 54, by = 0.5))))
ev_fig2 <- lapply(seq_along(fig2_doses), function(i) {
  rxode2::et(amt = fig2_doses[i], cmt = "depot", id = i) |>
    rxode2::et(fig2_grid, cmt = "Cc", id = i) |>
    as.data.frame()
}) |>
  bind_rows()
sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_fig2, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(dose = paste(fig2_doses[id], "mg po"))

sim_fig2 |>
  select(dose, time, THC = Cc, `11-OH-THC` = Cc_11oh, `THC-COOH` = Cc_thccooh) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(dose, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-3, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model-predicted lines of Figure 2 of Li 2025."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

At 10 mg the typical THC peak is about 3.6 ng/mL near 1 h and the curve falls
to about 0.013 ng/mL by 24 h, 11-OH-THC peaks near 2.5 ng/mL at 2 h, and
THC-COOH peaks near 20 ng/mL at 2-3 h and is still about 13 ng/mL at 8 h, which
is what the solid lines of Figure 2 show.

# External validation regimen (Figure 4)

The authors validated against Goodwin 2006: 0.13, 0.157, 2.5 or 4.93 mg THC
three times daily for 5 days, with only two doses on the first day in the
2.5 mg group.

```{r fig4}
goodwin <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  dose = c(0.13, 0.157, 2.5, 4.93)
)
dose_times <- seq(0, by = 8, length.out = 15)
fig4_grid <- seq(0, 185, by = 0.25)
ev_fig4 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(goodwin)), function(i) {
  tt <- dose_times
  # 2.5 mg group: 14 doses, the third dose of day 1 omitted.
  if (goodwin$dose[i] == 2.5) tt <- setdiff(tt, 16)
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = tt, amt = goodwin$dose[i], evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = i, time = fig4_grid, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "Cc")
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_fig4, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(regimen = paste(goodwin$dose[id], "mg TID x 5 days"))

sim_fig4 |>
  select(regimen, time, THC = Cc, `11-OH-THC` = Cc_11oh, `THC-COOH` = Cc_thccooh) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(regimen, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-4, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model-simulated lines of Figure 4 of Li 2025."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Per se limit analysis (Figure 5, Table 2)

The paper simulated occasional users as a single oral dose and frequent users
as the same dose twice daily for 14 days, at 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 mg,
and counted the fraction of simulated plasma THC concentrations above 1.4,
2.8 and 7 ng/mL (the 1, 2 and 5 ng/mL whole-blood limits divided by 0.71)
between 1 and 8 h and between 8 and 24 h after the last dose (Equations 14 and
15).

The model is linear, so a dose of D mg gives exactly D times the 1 mg
profile for the same random-effect draw. Table 2 shows this: the 2.5 mg / 1.4
ng/mL cell equals the 5 mg / 2.8 ng/mL cell, and the 10 mg / 1.4 ng/mL cell
equals the 50 mg / 7 ng/mL cell. A single 200-subject cohort per usage pattern
at 1 mg, scaled by dose, therefore reproduces the paper's design, including
its shared draws across dose groups.

```{r per-se-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250117)
n_sub <- 200
win_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)

ev_occ <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(win_grid, cmt = "Cc") |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_sub))
last_dose <- 13 * 24 + 12
ev_freq <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "depot", ii = 12, addl = 27) |>
  rxode2::et(last_dose + win_grid, cmt = "Cc") |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_sub))

sim_occ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, ev_occ, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(user = "Occasional", tald = time)
sim_freq <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, ev_freq, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(user = "Frequent", tald = time - last_dose)

# rxode2 returns the per-endpoint simulated observation (residual error
# included) in `sim`; with observation rows on cmt = "Cc" that is THC.
sim_perse <- bind_rows(sim_occ, sim_freq) |>
  select(id, user, tald, ipred = Cc, obs = sim)
stopifnot(nrow(sim_perse) == 2 * n_sub * length(win_grid))
```

```{r fig5, fig.height = 5}
limits <- c(1.4, 2.8, 7)
sim_perse |>
  expand_grid(dose = c(2.5, 10, 50)) |>
  mutate(conc = ipred * dose) |>
  group_by(user, dose, tald) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(conc, 0.05), med = median(conc), hi = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(tald > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(tald)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(limit = factor(limits)),
    aes(yintercept = as.numeric(as.character(limit)), colour = limit),
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("darkred", "blue", "purple")) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1, xmax = 8, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "orange") +
  facet_grid(user ~ paste(dose, "mg")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after last dose (h)", y = "THC plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Per se limit\n(ng/mL plasma)",
    caption = paste(
      "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 simulated subjects (inter-study",
      "variability only). Compare Figure 5 of Li 2025."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r table2}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~limit, ~dose, ~occ_1_8, ~occ_8_24, ~freq_1_8, ~freq_8_24,
  1.4, 2.5, 2.0, 0, 4.9, 0.6,
  1.4, 5, 12.6, 0.1, 21.6, 4.3,
  1.4, 10, 32.8, 2.0, 43.9, 13.6,
  1.4, 20, 53.7, 11.5, 58.5, 27.7,
  1.4, 50, 67.9, 34.2, 69.3, 46.5,
  1.4, 100, 73.0, 48.7, 74.0, 60.7,
  2.8, 2.5, 0, 0, 0.2, 0,
  2.8, 5, 2.0, 0, 4.9, 0.6,
  2.8, 10, 12.6, 0.1, 21.6, 4.3,
  2.8, 20, 32.8, 2.0, 43.9, 13.6,
  2.8, 50, 58.3, 16.6, 61.7, 32.3,
  2.8, 100, 67.9, 34.2, 69.3, 46.5,
  7, 2.5, 0, 0, 0, 0,
  7, 5, 0, 0, 0, 0,
  7, 10, 0.7, 0, 2.3, 0.2,
  7, 20, 7.7, 0, 14.8, 2.6,
  7, 50, 32.8, 2.0, 43.9, 13.6,
  7, 100, 53.7, 11.5, 58.5, 27.7
) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(limit, dose), names_to = "cell", values_to = "paper") |>
  separate(cell, c("user", "w1", "w2"), sep = "_") |>
  mutate(
    user = ifelse(user == "occ", "Occasional", "Frequent"),
    window = paste0(w1, "-", w2, " h")
  ) |>
  select(-w1, -w2)

# Equations 14-15: share of simulated concentrations in the window above
# the limit. The 1 mg concentrations are scaled by dose (linear model).
windows <- list(`1-8 h` = c(1, 8), `8-24 h` = c(8, 24))
pct_above <- function(users, window, dose, limit, column) {
  rng <- windows[[window]]
  d <- sim_perse[sim_perse$user == users & sim_perse$tald >= rng[1] &
    sim_perse$tald <= rng[2], ]
  100 * mean(d[[column]] * dose > limit)
}

sim_table2 <- table2 |>
  mutate(
    sim_ipred = mapply(pct_above, user, window, dose, limit, "ipred"),
    sim_obs = mapply(pct_above, user, window, dose, limit, "obs")
  )

sim_table2 |>
  arrange(user, window, limit, dose) |>
  mutate(across(c(sim_ipred, sim_obs), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  select(
    `User` = user, `Window` = window, `Limit (ng/mL)` = limit,
    `Dose (mg)` = dose, `Paper (%)` = paper,
    `Simulated, no residual (%)` = sim_ipred,
    `Simulated, with residual (%)` = sim_obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Probability of impairment detection: Table 2 of Li 2025 against the packaged model.")
```

```{r table2-check}
abs_diff <- abs(sim_table2$sim_obs - sim_table2$paper)
# Centre of the comparison over all 72 cells. With 200 subjects per usage
# pattern the Monte-Carlo SE of a single cell is at most about 3.5 points
# (binomial, p = 0.5, n = 200); the cells share one cohort, so the median
# moves far less than that across seeds. Agreement in the high-dose
# cells is worse than this and is discussed below.
stopifnot(median(abs_diff) < 5)
# Ordering: detection never falls with dose at a fixed limit and window.
stopifnot(all(
  sim_table2 |>
    group_by(user, window, limit) |>
    arrange(dose, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    summarise(mono = all(diff(sim_obs) >= 0), .groups = "drop") |>
    pull(mono)
))
```

The median absolute difference from Table 2 across the 72 cells is
`r round(median(abs_diff), 1)` percentage points when proportional residual
error is included. The doses up to 20 mg agree well; at 50 and 100 mg
the simulated detection probabilities are higher than the published ones (for
example `r round(sim_table2$sim_obs[sim_table2$limit == 1.4 & sim_table2$dose == 100 & sim_table2$user == "Occasional" & sim_table2$window == "1-8 h"], 1)`%
against 73.0% for occasional users at 100 mg and 1.4 ng/mL). The published
values level off near 73% even though a 100 mg dose puts the typical
THC concentration above 1.4 ng/mL for the whole 1-8 h window, which implies
that about a quarter of the paper's simulated concentrations in that window
stayed below 1.4 ng/mL at any dose, i.e. more than 70-fold below the typical
value. The paper does not describe its simulation grid or how it
handled residual error, and a ceiling like that does not follow from the
Table 1 variances, so the discrepancy is recorded here rather than adjusted
for.

# PKNCA validation

The model is linear with no parallel elimination from THC, so every
milligram of bioavailable THC is cleared through `cl` into 11-OH-THC, and a
fraction `fm` of that through `cl_11oh` into THC-COOH. The total exposures are
therefore exact:

- AUC(0-inf) THC = F x Dose / CL_THC
- AUC(0-inf) 11-OH-THC = F x Dose / CL_11-OH-THC
- AUC(0-inf) THC-COOH = F x Fm x Dose / CL_THC-COOH

with F = 1 for intravenous doses. PKNCA on a typical-value simulation of a
10 mg oral dose and the 3.495 mg intravenous dose of Naef 2004 (study ID 9)
is checked against these values. The terminal half-life is about 200 h
(the slow return from adipose), so the grid runs to 1500 h.

```{r pknca}
nca_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.25), seq(50, 1500, by = 10))))
nca_arms <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:2,
  treatment = c("10 mg oral", "3.495 mg IV"),
  dose = c(10, 3.495),
  cmt = c("depot", "central"),
  f = c(0.144, 1)
)
ev_nca <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(nca_arms)), function(i) {
  rxode2::et(amt = nca_arms$dose[i], cmt = nca_arms$cmt[i], id = i) |>
    rxode2::et(nca_grid, cmt = "Cc", id = i) |>
    as.data.frame()
}) |>
  bind_rows()
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, ev_nca,
  returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
)

conc_nca <- sim_nca |>
  select(id, time, THC = Cc, `11-OH-THC` = Cc_11oh, `THC-COOH` = Cc_thccooh) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc") |>
  left_join(select(nca_arms, id, treatment), by = "id") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0))
stopifnot(all(sim_nca$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_nca$Cc)))

dose_nca <- nca_arms |>
  crossing(analyte = c("THC", "11-OH-THC", "THC-COOH")) |>
  mutate(time = 0) |>
  select(id, treatment, analyte, time, dose)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + analyte / id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, dose ~ time | treatment + analyte + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data))

nca_wide <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, analyte, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

pars <- c(cl = 87, cl_11oh = 80.4, cl_thccooh = 4.34, fm = 0.904)
nca_check <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(select(nca_arms, treatment, dose, f), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(
    auc_closed = 1000 * f * dose * case_when(
      analyte == "THC" ~ 1 / pars[["cl"]],
      analyte == "11-OH-THC" ~ 1 / pars[["cl_11oh"]],
      analyte == "THC-COOH" ~ pars[["fm"]] / pars[["cl_thccooh"]]
    ),
    pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf.obs / auc_closed - 1)
  )

nca_check |>
  mutate(across(c(cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life, auc_closed, pct_diff), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  select(
    Treatment = treatment, Analyte = analyte, `Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax,
    `Tmax (h)` = tmax, `t1/2 (h)` = half.life,
    `AUC0-inf PKNCA (ng*h/mL)` = aucinf.obs,
    `AUC0-inf closed form (ng*h/mL)` = auc_closed, `Difference (%)` = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA on typical-value profiles against the closed-form total exposure.")

# Same parameter draws on both sides; the residual is trapezoid and
# extrapolation error on a 0.25 h / 10 h grid, measured below 0.5%.
stopifnot(all(abs(nca_check$pct_diff) < 2))
```

The paper reports no NCA summary, so the closed-form exposures are the
reference; the paper's own model-predicted curves are compared visually in
the Figure 2 and Figure 4 sections above.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Inter-study, not inter-individual, variability.** The four random effects
  were estimated across study means. They are encoded as ordinary etas so the
  model can be simulated the way the paper did for its 1000 virtual subjects,
  but they describe study-to-study spread of mean profiles, not
  subject-to-subject spread.
- **Residual error.** Equation 13 describes a combined proportional and
  additive model, but Table 1 reports only proportional variances for each
  analyte and no additive component. The model carries proportional error
  only, with SD = sqrt(sigma^2).
- **Supplement Table S3 disagrees on THC-COOH.** Its row for the final model
  (model 8) says "One-compartment for THC-COOH", while Figure 1, Equations 4
  and 11 and Table 1 (Q5, V_THC-COOH,peri) all describe two compartments. The
  equations and parameter table are followed.
- **Bioavailability.** Equation 1 starts the depot at the dose; F from Table 1
  is applied to the oral depot only. Intravenous doses go into `central`
  with F = 1, as the IV studies require.
- **Goodwin 2006 dose times.** The paper gives the sampling times but not the
  dose times. The Figure 4 replication assumes doses every 8 h from time 0,
  with the 16 h dose omitted in the 2.5 mg group to give 14 doses.
- **Per se simulation.** The grid of concentrations used for Equations 14 and
  15 is not stated; 0.25 h is used here. Table 2 is compared at 200 simulated
  subjects per usage pattern rather than the paper's 1000, and the
  high-dose cells disagree as described in that section.
- **Whole-blood to plasma.** The per se limits use the paper's 0.71
  blood:plasma ratio for THC; the model itself predicts plasma
  concentrations.
- **THC-COOH suffix.** The terminal metabolite uses the `thccooh` suffix
  (`central_thccooh`, `Cc_thccooh`), registered for this model.
